Definition: of Hebrew origin (H3063 or perhaps H3194); Judah (i.e. Jehudah or Juttah), a part of (or place in) Palestine:--Judah.
BiblicalUsage: Juda is the name of the land and the tribe, the country of the promise, and the Gospels use it where the place matters. In Matthew 2:6 Bethlehem stands in the land of Juda, in Luke 1:39 Mary goes into a city of Juda to greet Elisabeth, and in Hebrews 7:14 it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda, a tribe of which Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the land and the tribe are one promise: the Christ came out of Juda, from Bethlehem in the land of Juda, and no other tribe could have given him.
RelatedPeople: Judah; Jesus; Mary, Mother of Jesus
RelatedEvents: The Birth of Jesus; Mary Visits Elizabeth; The Magi Visit Jesus
